# Verifying Homer contracts on Elysium (chain 99901)

Every Homer contract below was built from this source with one set of settings. The file `out/verify/standard-input.json` (written by `npm run build && npm run verify-input`) holds every source and import with those exact settings: upload it as **Solidity (Standard JSON input)** on the explorer, pick the contract name, paste its constructor arguments, and submit.

- Compiler: **v0.8.28+commit.7893614a**
- Optimizer: enabled, 200 runs · viaIR: **yes** · EVM version: **shanghai** · metadata hash: **none**
- License: see each source file

All seven were checked on Nov 9, 2026: today's build gives exactly the creation code each one was deployed with (constructor arguments aside).

**Status: all seven verified on Nov 9, 2026 on Kinetiq's official explorer, https://elysium.kinetiq.xyz** (source and ABI published). The build sets `bytecodeHash: none`, so the bytecode carries no metadata hash and the explorer shows a partial match: the code is identical, only the metadata link is absent. They were submitted through its Etherscan-compatible API, `https://elysium.kinetiq.xyz/api` (`module=contract&action=verifysourcecode`, `codeformat=solidity-standard-json-input`), which is what `forge verify-contract --verifier etherscan --verifier-url https://elysium.kinetiq.xyz/api` does too.

## Not included

- **$HOMER token** (`0x365be4728d0ee2140e8b75a05c5dcf6b7d76399a`): launched on a launchpad, whose contract it is (fixed 1B supply, no owner, no minting). `src/HomerToken.sol` here is the plain fixed-supply token the fork tests stake with; it is not the deployed $HOMER.
- **Earlier LP managers** (retired versions): built from older sources; verify from the commit they were deployed from if needed.
